misconceptions.evidence: Built on documented surd errors: square factor taken out unrooted (25√2), stopping at a non-largest square (3√8), splitting a non-square factor (√12 = 6√2), outside and inside numbers swapped, √a + √b = √(a + b), adding the radicands of like surds (5√6), leaving a product under the root, halving instead of rooting, forgetting to divide when rationalising, and dropping the root.

lab_distinct.evidence: The square of area n is sliced into a k × k grid; only grids whose cells have whole areas work, the cell area m becomes the surd and the side is k cells of √m. Extra modes build a square back up from cells and cut a √2 square to area 1. Nearest flagship shingle similarity 3.9% (flag_rad.js), then 3.4% (flag_arc.js).

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners try grids before the rule is stated: dashed red grids show 12 ÷ 9 is not whole, 2 × 2 cells of 3 give 2√3; on 72 the 3 × 3 grid is flagged amber because 8 still splits, pushing on to 6 × 6; building 3√5 shows the 3 returns as 9 cells; the strip of area 1 is visibly half the √2 square, so 1/√2 = √2/2.

predictions.evidence: Five predicts, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 6√2 or 3√4 for √12, 25√2 or 10√5 for √50, 3√8 or 36√2 for √72, √15 or √35 for 3√5, and 1/2 or √2 for 1/√2; the correct option sits in different positions.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Played 24 answers in the browser across simplify, add, multiply and rationalise: 25√2 and 4√10 name the unrooted square, √68/√58 name √a + √b ≠ √(a + b) with the √9 + √16 counterexample, 64 names the product left under the root, 15√5 names the missing division by 5; each message ends with the full working.

readability.evidence: Flesch–Kincaid grade 0.5 for the kid text and 7.0 for the adult text (limits 6.5 and 9.5); kid text uses one idea per sentence with a picture (side of a square, four smaller squares, apples) and task lines are single instructions.

no_filler.evidence: Filler check passes and explanation overlap with all other lessons is 0%; the adult paragraphs cover the product rule and simplest form, largest square plus the reverse direction, like surds and rationalising, then the named slips, with no repeated template text.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 and 360 px Android screenshots of all seven steps show the grid, cell labels, side label, track and strip labels inside the canvas; real pointer drags on the phone viewport along the grid track to 6 × 6 and up the strip to area 1 both completed their tasks; a clearer h = 1/√2 = √2/2 label was added after a screenshot review.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs axe-core WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark on phone and desktop with no console errors; grid ± 1, cell ± 1, strip ± 1/± 5 and n ± 1 buttons with aria-labels replace every drag, and the canvas aria-label states the grid, cell area, and the resulting surd or why the grid fails.
